rules.text: If the query image shows a variation in color (e.g., liquid or wire) or label icon that matches a known product variant described in the reference profiler, trust A (Agent) to correctly identify it as normal.
If the query image contains a subtle, non-structural feature like printed text or markings on a component that is absent in all reference images, trust A (Agent) to detect this as a logical anomaly.
If the query image shows a clear physical defect such as a torn label, missing object, or extra foreign object, trust B (Direct) to correctly identify it as an anomaly.

If the query image shows a change in the count of components (e.g., extra washer, missing nut) or a change in the configuration of parts (e.g., number of terminal blocks), trust B (Direct) to detect this as a logical anomaly.

If the query image shows a change in the state of a product (e.g., liquid color change to an unexpected color like milky white) that is not a known variant, trust B (Direct) to identify it as an anomaly.
The bag contains exactly 2 bolts, 2 hexagonal nuts, and 2 flat washers.
The bag features a vertical resealable zipper strip on the right edge with repeating white recycling symbols.
The hardware components are metallic silver, and the bag is translucent dark grey/black.
Exactly two connector assemblies are present in the image.
Each connector assembly consists of exactly three vertically stacked units.
A single continuous cable connects the two connector assemblies.
The two connector assemblies are positioned on opposite sides of the image.
The connector bodies are orange and the cable is a solid color.
The background is a uniform metallic mesh pattern.
Exactly two distinct rectangular labels are present on the front face of the bottle.
The upper label is positioned in the vertical center of the bottle body, and the lower label is near the base.
The bottle has a clear glass body with a narrow neck and a screw-top cap.
Both labels feature a yellow background with black text or illustrations.
The container is a white, rectangular tray divided into two distinct compartments.
The left compartment contains exactly three whole fruits arranged vertically.
The right compartment is filled with granola in the top half and dried fruit/nuts in the bottom half.
The left compartment contains exactly two oranges and one peach.
The container consists of exactly 15 compartments arranged in a 3x5 grid.
Every compartment contains exactly one pushpin.
Pushpin heads are solid yellow; pins are metallic silver; background is black.
Each pushpin consists of a cylindrical yellow head and a single straight metallic pin.
Flag as anomaly if the bag contains loose washers or nuts that are not threaded onto the bolts.
Flag as anomaly if the image contains only the background mesh with no splicing connectors or cables present.
Do not flag wire color variations (e.g., yellow, blue) as anomalies if the connector structure and count are intact.
Do not flag a single-wire assembly as an anomaly if the connector housing structure is consistent with the baseline.
Flag as anomaly if the main fruit label is completely missing from the bottle surface.
Flag as anomaly if the main label shows physical damage, such as tears or cut-off text.
Do not flag bottles where the fruit icon and liquid color differ from the reference, provided the label is intact.
Flag as anomaly if granola/cereal is on the left and fresh fruit is on the right, reversing the standard layout.
Flag as anomaly if any compartment is completely empty or contains more than two pins.
Treat random pin orientation and non-centered placement within a compartment as normal variation.
